questions.memo: Hanukkah lasts eight nights. One candle is added each night on the menorah, marking the miracle of light lasting eight days.

questions.question: Which is a common feature across MANY religious festivals?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which is a common feature across many religious festivals?
options: Gathering with family, sharing food, prayer or reflection
questions.expected: Gathering with family, sharing food, prayer or reflection
questions.memo: Family, food, prayer and reflection — these threads run through almost every religious festival. People are more alike than we sometimes think.

questions.question: Match festival to religion: Diwali
questions.ruby_prompt: Pictures: a lit-up oil lamp (diya), a Christmas tree, a crescent moon and star, a Star of David. Which picture shows Diwali?
questions.context: Pictures: a lit-up oil lamp (diya), a Christmas tree, a crescent moon and star, a Star of David
questions.expected: Lit-up oil lamp (diya)
questions.memo: Diyas — small oil lamps — are a signature of Diwali. They symbolise the victory of light over darkness.

questions.question: Lerato's friend invites her to celebrate Eid. The kind thing to do is:
questions.ruby_prompt: Lerato's friend invites her to celebrate Eid with her family. What's the kind thing to do?
options: Go with respect, dress modestly, and learn about it
Eat all the food without thanks
questions.expected: Go with respect, dress modestly, and learn about it
questions.memo: Visiting another family's festival is an honour. Modest dress, polite questions and saying thank you make it warm for everyone.

questions.question: Tell me one religious festival you know of and what it celebrates.
questions.ruby_prompt: Tell me one religious festival you know of and what it celebrates.
questions.expected: Christmas — the birth of Jesus in Christianity
questions.memo: Good answers: any festival — Christmas, Easter, Eid, Diwali, Hanukkah, Passover, Vesak — paired with what it celebrates.

questions.question: What is the Baha'i Naw-Rúz festival?
questions.ruby_prompt: What is the Baha'i Naw-Rúz festival?
options: The Baha'i New Year, celebrated around 21 March
questions.expected: The Baha'i New Year, celebrated around 21 March
questions.memo: Naw-Rúz means 'new day'. It's the Baha'i (and Persian) New Year, marking the start of spring in the Northern Hemisphere.

questions.question: Why might a school celebrate or learn about many religious festivals?
questions.ruby_prompt: Why might a school choose to celebrate or learn about many religious festivals?
options: To respect every learner's background and build understanding across the community
To pick one religion as best
questions.expected: To respect every learner's background and build understanding across the community
questions.memo: When a school honours many traditions, every child feels seen — and all children learn to see each other clearly. That is the SA we want.

LS.L5.PSW.T10.title: Safety measures at home and the environment
LS.L5.PSW.T10.description: Harmful household products and medication, fire safety.
LS.L5.PSW.T10.recovery_strategy: Concrete rules save lives. Build the learner's mental safety checklist around chemicals, medicines, fire and electricity.

questions.question: Which is a harmful household product?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which of these is a harmful household product?
questions.expected: Bleach or strong drain cleaner
questions.memo: Cleaning products with chemicals — bleach, drain cleaner, strong soaps — can burn skin and eyes and poison if swallowed.

questions.question: Where should medicines be stored?
questions.ruby_prompt: Where should medicines be stored at home?
options: Out of reach of young children — high up and locked if possible
On the floor next to the toys
questions.expected: Out of reach of young children — high up and locked if possible
questions.memo: Many children are poisoned each year from medicines they thought were sweets. Lock them up. Out of reach.

questions.question: If you swallow something poisonous, what should you do?
questions.ruby_prompt: If you swallow something poisonous, what should you do?
options: Tell an adult immediately and call the Poisons Information Centre or 10177
Wait to see if you feel sick
questions.expected: Tell an adult immediately and call the Poisons Information Centre or 10177
questions.memo: Speed saves lives in poisoning. SA Poisons Information Centre: 0861 555 777. Ambulance: 10177. Don't wait.

questions.question: True or false: Medicine should always be taken from an adult, not by yourself.
questions.ruby_prompt: True or false: Medicine should always be given to children by an adult, not taken by the child alone.
questions.expected: true
questions.memo: Yes. Even safe medicines can hurt at the wrong dose. Adults give children's medicine — always.

questions.question: What should you do FIRST if a small fire starts in the kitchen?
questions.ruby_prompt: What should you do first if a small fire starts in the kitchen?
options: Get everyone out and call for help (10177 or fire service)
Pour water on an oil fire
Watch it to see what happens
questions.expected: Get everyone out and call for help (10177 or fire service)
questions.memo: People first. Get out, get help. Don't fight a fire unless you are TRAINED and it's tiny.

questions.question: True or false: It is safe to put water on a burning paraffin (kerosene) fire.
questions.ruby_prompt: True or false: It is safe to put water on a burning paraffin fire.
questions.expected: false
questions.memo: Water on paraffin or oil makes the fire EXPLODE outward. Smother it (a heavy lid) or use sand. Better — get out and call for help.

questions.question: Sipho sees an open container of paraffin near a fire. The safest thing to do is:
questions.ruby_prompt: Sipho sees an open container of paraffin standing close to a cooking fire. What's the safest thing to do?
options: Move it far away from the fire — paraffin can catch fire easily
Pour it on the fire to make it bigger
questions.expected: Move it far away from the fire — paraffin can catch fire easily
questions.memo: Paraffin and other fuels catch fire easily. Keep them well away from flames. Many SA shack fires start this way.

questions.question: Which is a fire safety rule for the home?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which is a fire safety rule for the home?
options: Leave the stove on all day
Light candles in bedrooms before sleeping
questions.expected: Never leave food cooking unattended
questions.memo: Unattended cooking is the leading cause of house fires. Stay in the kitchen while cooking.

questions.question: If your clothes catch fire, you should:
questions.ruby_prompt: If your clothes ever catch fire, you should:
options: STOP, DROP and ROLL — to smother the flames
Run as fast as you can
questions.expected: STOP, DROP and ROLL — to smother the flames
questions.memo: STOP (don't run — running feeds the fire). DROP (to the ground). ROLL (to put it out). Cover your face. Then get help.

questions.question: Put these steps in order for what to do if your house is on fire.
questions.ruby_prompt: Put these in order for what to do if your house is on fire.
options: Close doors behind you to slow the fire
questions.expected: Get everyone out fast,Stay low — smoke rises,Close doors behind you to slow the fire,Call 10177 from outside
questions.memo: Out → low (smoke kills more than flames) → close doors to slow the spread → call from outside. Never go back in for stuff.

questions.question: Why are matches and lighters dangerous for younger children?
questions.ruby_prompt: Why are matches and lighters dangerous for younger children?
options: A small flame can start a big fire that can hurt people and burn down homes
questions.expected: A small flame can start a big fire that can hurt people and burn down homes
questions.memo: Matches and lighters belong with adults — never with toddlers or as toys. House fires often start with a child's curiosity.

questions.question: Which is a hidden danger of paraffin stoves and candles?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which is a hidden danger of paraffin stoves and candles?
options: They can be knocked over and start a fire
questions.expected: They can be knocked over and start a fire
questions.memo: Paraffin stoves and candles are common in SA homes without electricity. They are useful but cause many house fires when knocked over.

questions.question: True or false: You should never plug too many appliances into one socket.
questions.ruby_prompt: True or false: You should never plug too many appliances into one wall socket.
questions.expected: true
questions.memo: Yes — overloading sockets is a major cause of electrical fires. One or two plugs per outlet, no daisy-chained adapters.

questions.question: Karabo finds an old bottle with no label under the kitchen sink. She should:
questions.ruby_prompt: Karabo finds an old bottle with no label under the kitchen sink. She should:
options: Not touch it — show an adult and let them handle it
Drink it to find out what's inside
questions.expected: Not touch it — show an adult and let them handle it
questions.memo: Unlabelled bottles are the worst kind — could be anything. Adults can identify or dispose of them safely.

questions.question: Which is a safer way to use electricity?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which is the safer way to use electricity at home?
options: Keep cords away from water and don't touch sockets with wet hands
Use plugs while standing in water
questions.expected: Keep cords away from water and don't touch sockets with wet hands
questions.memo: Water + electricity = severe shock or death. Dry hands. Cords out of water. Never poke things into sockets.

questions.question: Tell me one fire safety rule.
questions.ruby_prompt: Tell me one fire safety rule.
questions.expected: Never leave a stove on without watching it
questions.memo: Good answers: don't leave cooking unattended, no candles in bedrooms, keep matches from young children, know how to STOP-DROP-ROLL, have an escape plan.

questions.question: If a small grease (oil) fire starts in a pan, the BEST move is:
questions.ruby_prompt: If a small grease fire starts in a pan on the stove, what's the best move?
options: Turn off the heat and cover the pan with a lid to smother it
Pick the pan up and run
questions.expected: Turn off the heat and cover the pan with a lid to smother it
questions.memo: Smothering removes the air the fire needs. Water turns oil into a fireball. Lid = safe. Water on oil = disaster.

questions.question: Which is a sign of carbon monoxide danger from a stove?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which is a sign of carbon monoxide danger from a stove?
options: Headaches, dizziness, sleepiness in everyone at home
questions.expected: Headaches, dizziness, sleepiness in everyone at home
questions.memo: Carbon monoxide is invisible and odourless but deadly. Ventilate when burning paraffin, coal or gas. If many people feel sick — get outside.

questions.question: What is the SA fire/ambulance number?
questions.ruby_prompt: What's the SA emergency number for fire and ambulance?
questions.memo: 10177 = fire/ambulance. 10111 = police. 112 from any mobile phone connects to emergency services.

questions.question: The most important safety rule about home dangers is:
questions.ruby_prompt: What's the most important safety rule about home dangers?
options: Tell a grown-up about anything that looks dangerous — and never play with chemicals, medicines or fire
questions.expected: Tell a grown-up about anything that looks dangerous — and never play with chemicals, medicines or fire
questions.memo: Adults are your safety partners. Tell them when something seems off. Never experiment with chemicals, medicines or flames yourself.

LS.L5.PSW.T11.title: Water as an important basic need
LS.L5.PSW.T11.description: Importance of water, different ways of saving water, protecting the quality of water.
LS.L5.PSW.T11.recovery_strategy: Connect water lessons to SA reality — droughts, dams, taps. Small habits add up; the learner can really make a difference.

questions.question: Why is water important to life?
questions.ruby_prompt: Why is water so important to life?
options: All living things — people, animals, plants — need water to survive
questions.expected: All living things — people, animals, plants — need water to survive
questions.memo: Water is essential for life — our bodies, our food, our environment. Without water, life cannot continue.

questions.question: About how much of a person's body is water?
questions.ruby_prompt: About how much of a person's body is water?
questions.expected: About 60%
questions.memo: Roughly 60% of our body weight is water. Children are a bit more — closer to 65%. That's why we feel ill so quickly when dehydrated.

questions.question: Which is a way to SAVE water at home?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which is a way to save water at home?
options: Take shorter showers and turn the tap off while brushing teeth
Wash one cup in lots of water
Water the garden in the hot midday sun
questions.expected: Take shorter showers and turn the tap off while brushing teeth
questions.memo: Small habits save a lot — a tap left on uses up to 9 litres a minute. Off when not in use = serious savings.

questions.question: True or false: South Africa is a water-scarce country.
questions.ruby_prompt: True or false: South Africa is a water-scarce country.
questions.expected: true
questions.memo: Yes — SA is one of the 30 most water-scarce countries. We get less rain than many countries. Saving water is a national habit.

questions.question: Which is a way to PROTECT water quality?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which is a way to protect water quality?
options: Don't throw rubbish or chemicals into rivers, dams or drains
Wash motor parts in the river
questions.expected: Don't throw rubbish or chemicals into rivers, dams or drains
questions.memo: What goes in the drain often ends up in our water. Keep chemicals and rubbish OUT — and use proper bins and waste sites.

questions.question: What can polluted water cause?
questions.ruby_prompt: What can polluted water cause?
options: Serious illnesses like diarrhoea, cholera and typhoid
questions.expected: Serious illnesses like diarrhoea, cholera and typhoid
questions.memo: Dirty water kills millions of people worldwide each year. Diarrhoea, cholera, typhoid — all from water that wasn't clean.

questions.question: If you're not sure if water is clean, you should:
questions.ruby_prompt: If you're not sure if water is clean to drink, you should:
options: Boil it for at least 1 minute before drinking
questions.expected: Boil it for at least 1 minute before drinking
questions.memo: Boiling water kills most germs. Even in emergencies, a one-minute boil is the safest way to clean water for drinking.

questions.question: Lerato leaves the tap running while brushing her teeth. About how much water can she waste in 2 minutes?
questions.ruby_prompt: Lerato leaves the tap running while she brushes for 2 minutes. About how much water can she waste?
questions.expected: Up to 18 litres
questions.memo: A running tap uses about 9 litres a minute. Turning it off saves nearly 20 litres per brush — many times a day.

questions.question: True or false: A small leak that drips can waste hundreds of litres a month.
questions.ruby_prompt: True or false: A small leak that drips can waste hundreds of litres a month.
questions.expected: true
questions.memo: Yes — a slow drip can waste over 100 litres a month. Many drips across many homes = a huge loss. Fix leaks fast.

questions.question: Which household activity uses the MOST water?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which everyday activity at home uses the most water?
questions.expected: Bathing or showering
questions.memo: Showers and baths are the big water-users. A short shower beats a bath, and beats a long shower.

questions.question: Sipho's family is collecting rainwater in a tank. This helps because:
questions.ruby_prompt: Sipho's family is collecting rainwater in a tank. Why is this helpful?
options: It reduces how much tap water they need for gardens or cleaning
questions.expected: It reduces how much tap water they need for gardens or cleaning
questions.memo: Rainwater harvesting is a smart SA habit — collected from the roof, stored in a tank, used for garden or cleaning. Saves municipal water.

questions.question: Put these in order for cleaning unsafe water in an emergency.
questions.ruby_prompt: Put these in order for cleaning unsafe water in an emergency.
options: Filter out big bits through a cloth
Boil the water for at least 1 minute
Store it in a clean covered container
questions.expected: Filter out big bits through a cloth,Boil the water for at least 1 minute,Let it cool,Store it in a clean covered container
questions.memo: Filter (removes dirt), boil (kills germs), cool, store covered. This sequence saves lives in floods, droughts and outages.

questions.question: Karabo's town goes on water restrictions during a drought. The community should:
questions.ruby_prompt: Karabo's town is on water restrictions because of a drought. What should the community do?
options: Follow the rules — short showers, no hosepipes, full washing loads only
Use even more water to be safe
questions.expected: Follow the rules — short showers, no hosepipes, full washing loads only
questions.memo: Drought rules protect everyone's share. Cape Town's 2018 'Day Zero' was avoided because people followed restrictions — small actions, huge result.

questions.question: Why are wetlands important for water?
questions.ruby_prompt: Why are wetlands — marshy land near rivers — important for water?
options: They filter water naturally and store it
questions.expected: They filter water naturally and store it
questions.memo: Wetlands are nature's water filters — plants and soil clean the water as it passes through. Protecting wetlands = cleaner rivers.

questions.question: True or false: Washing a car with a bucket uses less water than a hosepipe.
questions.ruby_prompt: True or false: Washing a car with a bucket uses less water than a hosepipe.
questions.expected: true
questions.memo: Yes — a hosepipe runs free; a bucket uses just what's in it. Bucket wins on water saving every time.

questions.question: Tell me one thing you can do to save water.
questions.ruby_prompt: Tell me one thing you can do to save water.
questions.expected: Turn off the tap while brushing teeth
questions.memo: Good answers: short showers, tap off while brushing, fix leaks, full machine loads only, bucket-wash cars, water plants early/late, rainwater tank.

questions.question: Why is water called a 'basic need'?
questions.ruby_prompt: Why do we call water a 'basic need'?
options: Without water, humans can survive only a few days — so it's essential, not optional
questions.expected: Without water, humans can survive only a few days — so it's essential, not optional
questions.memo: We can live weeks without food, but only days without water. Basic needs = things life cannot continue without.

questions.question: Mpho sees a cracked pipe leaking water into the street. She should:
questions.ruby_prompt: Mpho sees a cracked pipe leaking water into the street. She should:
options: Tell a parent or report it to the municipality so it can be fixed
questions.expected: Tell a parent or report it to the municipality so it can be fixed
questions.memo: Burst pipes waste huge amounts of clean water. Quick reporting (parent → municipality → repair) saves it for everyone.

questions.question: Which is BEST for the environment when watering a garden?
questions.ruby_prompt: What's best for the environment when watering a garden?
options: Water early morning or evening, with grey water or a bucket if possible
Water at midday in full sun
questions.expected: Water early morning or evening, with grey water or a bucket if possible
questions.memo: Midday water evaporates before plants drink it. Early or late is efficient. Grey water (used bath/dishwater) is great for hardy plants.

questions.question: The most important truth about water in SA is:
questions.ruby_prompt: What's the most important truth about water in South Africa?
options: It's precious and shared — every drop saved helps the whole community
questions.expected: It's precious and shared — every drop saved helps the whole community
questions.memo: Water is a shared resource in a water-scarce country. Saving water is patriotic, neighbourly and essential — all at once.

LS.L5.PSW.T12.title: Healthy eating for children
LS.L5.PSW.T12.description: South African Food-Based Dietary Guidelines, dietary needs of children, factors influencing food intake.
LS.L5.PSW.T12.recovery_strategy: Stay non-judgmental about favourite foods. Healthy = mostly good choices + room for treats. Frame food positively, not as 'good vs bad'.

questions.question: Which is the BIGGEST food group children should eat?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which food group should children eat the MOST of?
options: Starchy foods like pap, rice, bread, samp, potatoes
questions.expected: Starchy foods like pap, rice, bread, samp, potatoes
questions.memo: Starchy foods are the SA Dietary Guidelines' base — they give energy. Whole grains (brown bread, brown rice) are best.

questions.question: Which food group helps your body grow and repair?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which food group helps your body grow and repair itself?
options: Proteins — meat, fish, eggs, beans, peas, lentils, milk
questions.expected: Proteins — meat, fish, eggs, beans, peas, lentils, milk
questions.memo: Protein builds muscles, skin, blood and helps the body heal. Beans and lentils are affordable proteins — and very nutritious.

questions.question: Why do we need fruit and vegetables every day?
questions.ruby_prompt: Why do we need fruit and vegetables every day?
options: They give us vitamins, minerals and fibre that protect health
They make us taller in one day
questions.expected: They give us vitamins, minerals and fibre that protect health
questions.memo: Different colours = different vitamins. Aim for variety. The SA guideline: 'Eat plenty of vegetables and fruit every day.'

questions.question: True or false: Eating too much sugar can lead to tooth decay and other health problems.
questions.ruby_prompt: True or false: Eating too much sugar can lead to tooth decay and other health problems.
questions.expected: true
questions.memo: Yes — too much sugar causes tooth decay, obesity, and increases risk of diabetes. SA guideline: 'Use sugar and foods/drinks high in sugar sparingly.'

questions.question: Which drink is BEST for everyday thirst?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which drink is best for everyday thirst?
questions.expected: Plain water
questions.memo: Water is the body's first choice — no sugar, hydrates fully. SA guideline: 'Drink lots of clean, safe water.'

questions.question: Which factor INFLUENCES what children eat?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which factor often influences what children eat?
options: What's available at home, school and shop, plus what parents and friends eat
Only the colour of the food
Only the day of the week
questions.expected: What's available at home, school and shop, plus what parents and friends eat
questions.memo: What's around us shapes our diet — at home, at school, in our community. Knowing this helps us choose more wisely.

questions.question: Sipho often skips breakfast. The most common effect is:
questions.ruby_prompt: Sipho often skips breakfast. What's the most common effect?
options: Tired, hungry and trouble concentrating in class
questions.expected: Tired, hungry and trouble concentrating in class
questions.memo: Breakfast = brain fuel. Without it, focus drops, energy drops, mood drops. Even a simple porridge or bread + spread helps.

questions.question: Which is a HEALTHY school lunch idea?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which is a healthy school lunch idea?
options: Sandwich with protein (peanut butter or egg or chicken) + fruit + water
questions.expected: Sandwich with protein (peanut butter or egg or chicken) + fruit + water
questions.memo: Balanced lunch = energy + protein + vitamins. Keeps a learner going through the afternoon.

questions.question: Lerato has a peanut allergy. What should she do at the lunch table?
questions.ruby_prompt: Lerato has a peanut allergy. What should she do at the lunch table?
options: Check that food she shares doesn't contain peanuts and tell adults about her allergy
Eat peanut butter to test it
questions.expected: Check that food she shares doesn't contain peanuts and tell adults about her allergy
questions.memo: Food allergies can be life-threatening. Always check labels and ingredients. Adults at school need to know about allergies.

questions.question: Which is a sign of being well-fed and healthy?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which is a sign of being well-fed and healthy?
options: Steady energy through the day, healthy weight, growing as expected
questions.expected: Steady energy through the day, healthy weight, growing as expected
questions.memo: A well-fed child has energy for school, play and sleep. Doctors and nurses can also check growth on a chart at the clinic.

questions.question: Why is FIBRE important for children?
questions.ruby_prompt: Why is fibre important for children?
options: Fibre helps your tummy work well and keeps you regular
questions.expected: Fibre helps your tummy work well and keeps you regular
questions.memo: Fibre is in fruit skins, vegetables, beans, and whole grains. It keeps your digestion working and you feeling full.

questions.question: True or false: ALL children grow at exactly the same speed.
questions.ruby_prompt: True or false: All children grow at exactly the same speed.
questions.expected: false
questions.memo: Children grow at different speeds and reach milestones at different ages. Healthy eating + sleep + activity supports each one's own growth pattern.

questions.question: Karabo's family can't afford much meat. What's a good protein alternative?
questions.ruby_prompt: Karabo's family can't afford much meat. What's a good protein alternative?
options: Beans, lentils, peanut butter and eggs — affordable and full of protein
questions.expected: Beans, lentils, peanut butter and eggs — affordable and full of protein
questions.memo: Plant proteins are cheaper than meat and very nutritious. Sugar beans, lentils, chickpeas, peanut butter, eggs — all SA staples.

questions.question: Mpho ate a big bowl of pap, vegetables and a small piece of chicken. Her meal:
questions.ruby_prompt: Mpho ate pap, vegetables and a small piece of chicken. How balanced is her meal?
options: Balanced — it has starch, vegetables and protein
questions.expected: Balanced — it has starch, vegetables and protein
questions.memo: Three of the four key groups — starch + veg + protein. Add a glass of water and a fruit later and it's a healthy day.

questions.question: Put these foods in order from HEALTHIEST to least healthy as a daily snack.
questions.ruby_prompt: Put these foods in order, healthiest first, as a daily snack.
questions.expected: Apple,Plain biltong (in moderation),Sweet biscuit,Sweets
questions.memo: Fruit first. Lean protein next. Then less-bad treats. Then plain sugar. Daily ≠ always; treats are fine sometimes.

questions.question: Tell me a healthy meal you like.
questions.ruby_prompt: Tell me a healthy meal that you like to eat.
questions.expected: Pap with vegetables and chicken
questions.memo: Good answers: any meal with a starch + a protein + vegetables. SA examples: pap + stew, samp and beans + spinach, rice + curry + salad.

questions.question: Why do children need MORE food per kilo of body weight than adults?
questions.ruby_prompt: Why do children sometimes need more food per kilogram of body weight than adults?
options: Children are growing and use a lot of energy for growth and activity
questions.expected: Children are growing and use a lot of energy for growth and activity
questions.memo: Growth + activity = high energy needs. That's why a small child can eat surprisingly large amounts and still be healthy.

questions.question: Which factor does NOT influence what children eat?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which of these does NOT influence what children eat?
options: The day of the week's number
questions.expected: The day of the week's number
questions.memo: Money, family, friends, ads, culture — all real influences. The day-number does not. Knowing influences helps us see why we choose what we do.

questions.question: True or false: It's okay to have a sweet treat sometimes, not every day.
questions.ruby_prompt: True or false: It's okay to have a sweet treat sometimes, just not every day.
questions.expected: true
questions.memo: Healthy eating allows for treats. The key is OCCASIONALLY, not daily. Restricting completely often makes treats more appealing — balance is better.

questions.question: What's the BIG idea of healthy eating?
questions.ruby_prompt: What's the big idea of healthy eating?
options: Eat a variety of foods from all groups, mostly whole foods, with water as the main drink
questions.expected: Eat a variety of foods from all groups, mostly whole foods, with water as the main drink
questions.memo: Variety + balance + water. That's the heart of the SA Dietary Guidelines. Whole foods over packaged ones, most of the time.

LS.L5.PSW.T13.title: Local environmental health problems
LS.L5.PSW.T13.description: Locally occurring health problems (tuberculosis, diarrhoea, malaria, measles etc.) — causes, symptoms, available treatment.
LS.L5.PSW.T13.recovery_strategy: Focus on prevention and where to get help. SA has free public clinics and well-known prevention practices — keep tone hopeful and practical.

questions.question: What is TUBERCULOSIS (TB)?
questions.ruby_prompt: What is tuberculosis — TB?
options: A serious lung disease caused by germs (bacteria) that spreads through coughing
questions.expected: A serious lung disease caused by germs (bacteria) that spreads through coughing
questions.memo: TB attacks the lungs and spreads through the air when an infected person coughs. SA has one of the highest TB rates in the world.

questions.question: What is the main symptom of TB?
questions.ruby_prompt: What's the main symptom of TB?
options: A cough that lasts more than 2 weeks, often with night sweats and weight loss
questions.expected: A cough that lasts more than 2 weeks, often with night sweats and weight loss
questions.memo: Long cough + night sweats + weight loss = see a clinic. TB is curable with the right medicine — but you have to start.

questions.question: Is TB curable?
questions.ruby_prompt: Is TB curable?
options: Yes — with the right medicine taken every day for 6 months, free at SA clinics
questions.expected: Yes — with the right medicine taken every day for 6 months, free at SA clinics
questions.memo: TB is curable. SA clinics give the medicine for free. Taking it every single day for the full course is critical.

questions.question: What causes most cases of DIARRHOEA in children?
questions.ruby_prompt: What causes most cases of diarrhoea in children?
options: Germs from dirty water or unwashed hands
questions.expected: Germs from dirty water or unwashed hands
questions.memo: Diarrhoea spreads through the mouth — from dirty water, food, or hands. Washing hands and clean water prevent most cases.

questions.question: What is the main treatment for diarrhoea in children?
questions.ruby_prompt: What's the main treatment for diarrhoea in children?
options: Plenty of fluids and an oral rehydration solution (ORS)
questions.expected: Plenty of fluids and an oral rehydration solution (ORS)
questions.memo: Diarrhoea drains water and salts from the body. ORS sachets (free at clinics) replace them and save lives.

questions.question: What spreads MALARIA?
questions.ruby_prompt: What spreads malaria?
options: The bite of a specific kind of mosquito
questions.expected: The bite of a specific kind of mosquito
questions.memo: Malaria spreads through mosquito bites — mostly in low-lying parts of Limpopo, Mpumalanga and KZN. Mosquito nets and repellent help.

questions.question: Which is a way to PREVENT malaria?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which is a way to prevent malaria?
options: Sleep under a mosquito net and use repellent in malaria areas
questions.expected: Sleep under a mosquito net and use repellent in malaria areas
questions.memo: Nets and repellent reduce mosquito bites dramatically. If you live in or visit a malaria area, take prevention seriously.

questions.question: What is MEASLES?
questions.ruby_prompt: What is measles?
options: A serious viral disease that causes a fever and a red rash, especially in children
questions.expected: A serious viral disease that causes a fever and a red rash, especially in children
questions.memo: Measles is highly contagious and can be deadly. Vaccination protects children — and is free at SA clinics.

questions.question: Which prevents measles?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which prevents measles?
options: The measles vaccine (given as part of the EPI — Expanded Programme on Immunisation)
questions.expected: The measles vaccine (given as part of the EPI — Expanded Programme on Immunisation)
questions.memo: The measles vaccine, given to all SA children for free, prevents measles. Catch-up vaccines are also free for older children who missed them.

questions.question: True or false: Vaccines protect children from many dangerous diseases.
questions.ruby_prompt: True or false: Vaccines protect children from many dangerous diseases.
questions.expected: true
questions.memo: Yes. Vaccines have saved millions of children's lives. SA's free public vaccine programme covers measles, TB, polio, hepatitis and more.

questions.question: Where can you get free vaccines in South Africa?
questions.ruby_prompt: Where can you get free vaccines in South Africa?
options: Only one hospital in the country
questions.expected: Any government clinic
questions.memo: Government clinics in every district offer free vaccines. The Road to Health booklet records every vaccine your child has had.

questions.question: Sipho's friend has a cough that won't go away after 3 weeks. He should:
questions.ruby_prompt: Sipho's friend has had a cough that won't go away for 3 weeks. What should he do?
options: See a clinic — a long cough could be TB and needs testing
questions.expected: See a clinic — a long cough could be TB and needs testing
questions.memo: Two-plus weeks of coughing is a red flag for TB. Clinics test for free. Early treatment saves lives and stops spread.

questions.question: Which is a way to prevent diarrhoea in a family?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which is a way to prevent diarrhoea in a family?
options: Wash hands, drink clean water, cook food well, cover food
questions.expected: Wash hands, drink clean water, cook food well, cover food
questions.memo: Four habits prevent most cases. They're simple, free and effective.

questions.question: Karabo's baby brother has bad diarrhoea for 2 days. The family should:
questions.ruby_prompt: Karabo's baby brother has bad diarrhoea for 2 days. What should the family do?
options: Take him to the clinic urgently — babies dehydrate fast and need ORS
questions.expected: Take him to the clinic urgently — babies dehydrate fast and need ORS
questions.memo: Babies and small children dehydrate dangerously fast. Diarrhoea in babies = clinic now. ORS often saves the day.

questions.question: Put these steps in order for going to the clinic when you feel sick.
questions.ruby_prompt: Put these in order for going to the clinic when you feel sick.
options: Notice the symptoms (cough, fever, rash, diarrhoea)
Tell a parent or trusted adult
Take any medicine exactly as told
questions.expected: Notice the symptoms (cough, fever, rash, diarrhoea),Tell a parent or trusted adult,Visit the local clinic,Take any medicine exactly as told
questions.memo: Notice → tell → clinic → follow instructions. Skipping medicine doses or stopping early is how diseases come back, sometimes stronger.

questions.question: True or false: TB can be passed by sharing a meal with someone (eating from the same plate).
questions.ruby_prompt: True or false: TB can be passed by sharing a meal from the same plate.
questions.expected: false
questions.memo: TB spreads through the AIR (coughing, sneezing), not through food. Sharing food doesn't spread TB. (Wash hands anyway — for other reasons.)

questions.question: Why is COVERING YOUR MOUTH when coughing important?
questions.ruby_prompt: Why is covering your mouth when coughing important?
options: It stops you from spreading germs to others
questions.expected: It stops you from spreading germs to others
questions.memo: Cough into your elbow (not hands — they spread germs to door handles, food). Saves others from your cold/flu/TB.

questions.question: Tell me one disease and one way to prevent it.
questions.ruby_prompt: Tell me one disease and one way to prevent it.
questions.expected: Diarrhoea — wash hands before eating
questions.memo: Good answers: TB (cover your mouth when coughing); diarrhoea (clean water, hand-washing); malaria (mosquito nets); measles (vaccine).

questions.question: Mpho's family doesn't have clean drinking water. The safest thing to do is:
questions.ruby_prompt: Mpho's family doesn't have clean drinking water. The safest thing to do is:
options: Boil all water for at least 1 minute or use water-purification tablets from a clinic
questions.expected: Boil all water for at least 1 minute or use water-purification tablets from a clinic
questions.memo: Boiling is the cheapest disinfection. Free water-purification tablets are available at many clinics in places with water problems.

questions.question: What's the most important thing to know about local health problems?
questions.ruby_prompt: What's the most important thing to know about local health problems?
options: Most can be prevented or treated — early help at a clinic saves lives
questions.expected: Most can be prevented or treated — early help at a clinic saves lives
questions.memo: Prevention + early treatment = the SA public health story. Free clinics, free vaccines, free TB medicine — use them, share them.

LS.L5.PSW.T14.title: HIV and AIDS: dealing with stigma
LS.L5.PSW.T14.description: Stigma about HIV and AIDS; how to change attitudes towards people infected with HIV and AIDS.
LS.L5.PSW.T14.recovery_strategy: Lead with facts; correct myths gently, not shamefully. Reinforce: HIV is a virus, not a moral failing. People with HIV deserve full friendship and dignity.

questions.question: What is 'stigma'?
questions.ruby_prompt: What does the word 'stigma' mean?
options: When people are unfairly judged or shunned because of something about them
questions.expected: When people are unfairly judged or shunned because of something about them
questions.memo: Stigma is when society marks someone as 'less than' for something — an illness, race, religion, identity. It hurts the person and isolates them.

questions.question: Stigma around HIV often comes from:
questions.ruby_prompt: Stigma around HIV often comes from what?
options: Old myths, fear, and lack of accurate information
questions.expected: Old myths, fear, and lack of accurate information
questions.memo: When people don't know how HIV actually spreads, fear fills the gap with myths. Real information ends stigma.

questions.question: True or false: People with HIV are NORMAL people who happen to have a virus.
questions.ruby_prompt: True or false: People with HIV are normal people who happen to have a virus.
questions.expected: true
questions.memo: Yes. HIV is a virus — like flu or measles, only specific in how it spreads. Having it doesn't change who someone is as a person.

questions.question: A student with HIV joins your class. The right attitude is:
questions.ruby_prompt: A new classmate with HIV joins your class. What's the right attitude?
options: Welcome them like any other classmate — they can't infect you in everyday school life
questions.expected: Welcome them like any other classmate — they can't infect you in everyday school life
questions.memo: HIV doesn't spread through everyday school life — sharing pencils, food, desks, hugs, sport. Welcoming them is right AND safe.

questions.question: Stigma can affect a person with HIV by:
questions.ruby_prompt: Stigma can affect a person with HIV by:
options: Making them afraid to get tested or take medicine — which makes them sicker
questions.expected: Making them afraid to get tested or take medicine — which makes them sicker
questions.memo: Stigma is dangerous — people hide their status, skip testing, skip treatment. Ending stigma is part of ending HIV.

questions.question: Which is a way to FIGHT stigma?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which is a way to fight stigma against people with HIV?
options: Share accurate facts and treat everyone with respect
questions.expected: Share accurate facts and treat everyone with respect
questions.memo: Stigma falls when facts are loud and respect is daily. Each kind action, each correct fact, weakens stigma.

questions.question: True or false: You can catch HIV from sitting next to someone with HIV in class.
questions.ruby_prompt: True or false: You can catch HIV from sitting next to someone with HIV in class.
questions.expected: false
questions.memo: False — HIV is not spread by sitting, sharing air, touching desks, eating together. The fear is the myth, not the science.

questions.question: Lerato's aunt is on ARVs. Lerato sees her aunt take her pills every day. This is because:
questions.ruby_prompt: Lerato's aunt is on ARVs and takes them every day. Why does she do this?
options: Daily ARVs keep HIV under control so she can stay healthy and not spread the virus
questions.expected: Daily ARVs keep HIV under control so she can stay healthy and not spread the virus
questions.memo: ARVs taken daily reduce HIV to almost zero in the blood — that's called 'undetectable'. Aunt stays well, and the virus can't pass on.

questions.question: Sipho hears a classmate saying mean things about a child with HIV. What should Sipho do?
questions.ruby_prompt: Sipho hears a classmate saying mean things about a child with HIV. What should Sipho do?
options: Speak up calmly with the facts and tell a teacher
questions.expected: Speak up calmly with the facts and tell a teacher
questions.memo: Allies matter. Speaking up — with facts, not anger — protects the person being targeted and changes the room.

questions.question: What does U=U mean (in HIV)?
questions.ruby_prompt: What does U=U mean in HIV?
options: Undetectable = Untransmittable — when HIV in the blood is very low, it cannot be passed on
questions.expected: Undetectable = Untransmittable — when HIV in the blood is very low, it cannot be passed on
questions.memo: U=U is one of the biggest scientific discoveries in HIV. With proper ARVs, the virus level drops so low it can't pass — a game-changer.

questions.question: Why is HIV testing important?
questions.ruby_prompt: Why is HIV testing important?
options: So people can start treatment early and stay healthy — and so they don't unknowingly pass it on
questions.expected: So people can start treatment early and stay healthy — and so they don't unknowingly pass it on
questions.memo: Testing is power. Knowing your status lets you start ARVs early — and protect those you love. Free at all SA clinics.

questions.question: Karabo's friend just told her she has HIV. Karabo should:
questions.ruby_prompt: Karabo's friend has just told her she has HIV. What should Karabo do?
options: Thank her for trusting her, keep being a good friend, and keep the info private
questions.expected: Thank her for trusting her, keep being a good friend, and keep the info private
questions.memo: Telling someone you have HIV takes courage. The right response is steady friendship + privacy. The friend doesn't suddenly become 'different'.

questions.question: True or false: Children born to mothers with HIV can be born HIV-negative.
questions.ruby_prompt: True or false: Children born to mothers with HIV can be born HIV-negative with proper care.
questions.expected: true
questions.memo: Yes — with proper medical care, mothers with HIV can have HIV-negative babies. SA's mother-to-child prevention programme is one of the most successful in the world.

questions.question: A myth says HIV can be cured by certain herbs or rituals. The truth is:
questions.ruby_prompt: A myth says HIV can be cured by certain herbs or rituals. What's the truth?
options: HIV has no cure yet — but ARVs control it so people live long healthy lives
questions.expected: HIV has no cure yet — but ARVs control it so people live long healthy lives
questions.memo: No cure exists yet. But ARVs are real medicine that works. False 'cures' cost people their health and lives by delaying treatment.

questions.question: Mpho refuses to share a pencil with a classmate she heard has HIV. The right thing is:
questions.ruby_prompt: Mpho refuses to share a pencil with a classmate she heard has HIV. What is the right thing?
options: Sharing a pencil is completely safe — HIV doesn't spread that way. Mpho's behaviour is stigma
questions.expected: Sharing a pencil is completely safe — HIV doesn't spread that way. Mpho's behaviour is stigma
questions.memo: Stigma often shows up in tiny acts — not sharing a pencil, not sitting near. Each one tells the person they're 'less than'. Knowing the facts ends it.

questions.question: Tell me one way to show kindness to a person with HIV.
questions.ruby_prompt: Tell me one way to show kindness to a person with HIV.
questions.expected: Treat them the same as anyone else — play with them, listen, care
questions.memo: Good answers: be a friend, listen if they want to talk, keep their info private, correct myths around you, sit with them at lunch.

questions.question: World AIDS Day is on:
questions.ruby_prompt: What date is World AIDS Day?
questions.expected: 1 December each year
questions.memo: 1 December — the world remembers people who have died of AIDS and renews the fight against HIV. The red ribbon is the symbol.

questions.question: Why might someone with HIV not tell anyone about their status?
questions.ruby_prompt: Why might a person with HIV not tell anyone about their HIV status?
options: Fear of stigma — being judged, gossiped about or rejected
Because they don't know the facts
questions.expected: Fear of stigma — being judged, gossiped about or rejected
questions.memo: Stigma is the reason for the silence. Making communities safer to disclose = saving lives. Each of us shapes that.

questions.question: Put these in order for SUPPORTING a friend who has just told you they have HIV.
questions.ruby_prompt: Put these in order for supporting a friend who just told you they have HIV.
options: Listen and thank them for trusting you
Treat them the same as before
Stand up for them if others are unkind
questions.expected: Listen and thank them for trusting you,Keep their info private,Treat them the same as before,Stand up for them if others are unkind
questions.memo: Listen → confidentiality → continuity → allyship. Each step says: 'You are not alone, and you are still you.'

questions.question: The MOST important truth to remember about people with HIV is:
questions.ruby_prompt: What's the most important truth to remember about people with HIV?
options: They are full people, deserve full dignity, and can live long healthy lives with treatment
questions.expected: They are full people, deserve full dignity, and can live long healthy lives with treatment
questions.memo: Full people. Full dignity. Full lives. With ARVs widely available in SA, HIV is a treatable condition, not a tragedy.

LS.L5.PSW.T15.title: Substance abuse
LS.L5.PSW.T15.description: Types of legal and illegal drugs including tobacco, alcohol and over-the-counter medication; negative impact of substances on body and mind.
LS.L5.PSW.T15.recovery_strategy: Be factual about harm without moralising. Reinforce: addiction is an illness, not a character flaw. Help is real — trusted adults, school counsellors, SANCA.

questions.question: What is 'substance abuse'?
questions.ruby_prompt: What is substance abuse?
options: Using a drug, alcohol or other substance in a harmful way
questions.expected: Using a drug, alcohol or other substance in a harmful way
questions.memo: Substance abuse = harmful use of substances that affect the brain and body — illegal drugs, alcohol, tobacco, or even some medicines.

questions.question: Which is a LEGAL drug that still harms health?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which is a legal drug that still harms health?
questions.expected: Tobacco (cigarettes) and alcohol
questions.memo: Legal ≠ safe. Tobacco kills millions worldwide; alcohol harms the body in many ways. Legal for adults under control, never for children.

questions.question: What does tobacco mostly harm?
questions.ruby_prompt: What does tobacco mostly harm in the body?
options: The lungs, heart and blood vessels
questions.expected: The lungs, heart and blood vessels
questions.memo: Tobacco causes lung cancer, heart disease, strokes. Half of all smokers die of a smoking-related illness.

questions.question: What does alcohol do to the brain?
questions.ruby_prompt: What does alcohol do to the brain?
options: Slows it down, affects thinking, balance and judgement
questions.expected: Slows it down, affects thinking, balance and judgement
questions.memo: Alcohol is a depressant — slows the brain. That's why drunk drivers crash, fall, fight. Children's brains still developing are at extra risk.

questions.question: True or false: Children's bodies are MORE damaged by alcohol than adult bodies.
questions.ruby_prompt: True or false: Children's bodies are more damaged by alcohol than adult bodies.
questions.expected: true
questions.memo: Yes. A child's body and brain are still growing. Alcohol does long-term harm. Legal age for alcohol in SA is 18 for this reason.

questions.question: Which is an ILLEGAL drug?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which of these is an illegal drug?
questions.expected: Tik, dagga (in many situations), heroin
questions.memo: Many street drugs are illegal in SA. They damage the brain, body and life chances. Avoiding them is the strongest move you can make.

questions.question: What is 'addiction'?
questions.ruby_prompt: What is addiction?
options: When someone can't stop using a substance even though it's hurting them
questions.expected: When someone can't stop using a substance even though it's hurting them
